examples.title: A defensible one-page outline
examples.situation: A 100 m² sandy-loam plot has OM 0.8%, EC 3.5 dS/m without an extraction method and slightly saline borewell water.
reasoning: Concern 1: low measured OM may limit storage; test soil and amendment quality before a rate.
Concern 2: possible salt stress needs method-matched ECe, depth and drainage evidence.
Concern 3: borewell water needs ECw and ion analysis before an irrigation/leaching plan.
Put tests, conditional interventions, crop candidates and monitoring on one page.
examples.takeaway: Do not declare a final crop or compost/leaching dose from the incomplete report.

examples.title: Preserve the model's quantities without adopting them blindly
examples.situation: The teacher model says 5–10 cm compost/manure, mixed through 15 cm of soil, and 7–10 cm straw/wood-chip mulch. The bank model says 15–20 cm incorporation and 5–10 cm mulch for a different sandy, alkaline scenario.
reasoning: These are different source examples, not a validated prescription for the pilot plot.
At 100 m², a 5 cm surface layer alone occupies 5 m³; a 10 cm layer occupies 10 m³ before shrinkage, density and mixing, demonstrating why material supply and analysis matter.
Ask for product EC, nutrients, maturity, target crop, soil results, budget and safe incorporation depth.
examples.takeaway: Retain both original example ranges in the learning record; obtain a documented site specification before field application.

examples.title: Barley plus sorghum as conditional candidates
examples.situation: A student proposes barley for possible salinity tolerance and sorghum for drought adaptation on the small plot.
reasoning: Barley has a relatively high salt-tolerance rating for grain in an FAO reference, but seedling establishment can be less tolerant.
Sorghum can be drought adapted and is only moderately salt tolerant in the same comparison; these are different reasons, not interchangeable ratings.
Before a decision, confirm ECe/ECw, cultivar, season, seed supply, establishment water and expected use.
examples.takeaway: A justified preliminary pair, not a promise of successful yield; cowpea, quinoa, sugar beet and other source candidates need their own checks.

examples.title: A third technique depends on the site
examples.situation: For a sandy, alkaline case, a student proposes compost, straw mulch and a vetch cover crop plus a tree windbreak.
reasoning: Compost quality and salinity must be checked before a rate; it cannot be assumed to correct pH or salt.
Mulch may reduce evaporation, but the material and depth depend on crop and irrigation.
Vetch and windbreaks need water and space; a very dry 100 m² pilot may have better alternatives.
examples.takeaway: Give three distinct techniques with conditional reasons and explain why one option may be deferred.
